passages.title: A Rose
passages.text:
It was a lovely summer morning. An eight-year-old girl, Suzzanna was taking a walk with her elder sister, Jane on a *path in the village they lived in. They saw a woman (1) (ア walk / イ walked / ウ walking / エ was walking) with a small dog. Suzzanna said to Jane, “Both the woman and the dog look very happy. Do you think we could have a puppy?” “Well, it is a difficult question. You must speak to Mum,” Jane said. “Okay. I will ask her. I think she will tell me a good answer.”

Next day Suzzanna saw her mother in the kitchen and said to her, “Mum, I saw a dog yesterday. I have wanted to have a dog since I was a little girl. Can I have one? If possible, I want a female one.” Then her mother said, “You are still a little girl. You are (2) (　　　) old enough to look after a dog. Wait until you become older.” “Why can’t I have a dog? I can feed her, take her for a walk, and brush her. I can do everything.” “I’m sorry, Suzzanna. As I told you, you are a bit too young. You must wait for a few years.” “I’m not too young! Why do I have to wait?” Suzzanna said angrily. Then she ran toward the front door and out of the house.

Suzzanna *held back tears and started walking toward the local park. When she came to the path near the park, she saw an elderly woman (3) (　　　) was lying on the ground. She went to the woman and said, “Are you all right?” The old woman said, “Yes, I think so. I slipped and fell.” Suzzanna held the woman’s hands and helped her stand up. The woman said, “Oh, thank you very much, young lady.” “Not at all,” Suzzanna said. “May I give you this for your kindness?” the woman said and handed a rose to Suzzanna. She became very happy and said, “Thank you very much. I will take it home.”

Suzzanna forgot about having a dog and walked back home. When she got home, she told her mother about the elderly woman and the rose. “Mum, can I keep this rose in a small vase?” Suzzanna’s mother said, “Yes, it’s a good idea. But how about planting it in the garden?” Suzzanna said, “You’re joking. Does this rose grow?” “I’m not joking. Cut the flower and keep only top leaves. Cut off the rest of the leaves and plant the *stem. It may grow.”

Though she was not sure, she followed her mother’s instructions and planted the stem in the garden and then watered it. Next morning she went to the *spot and found that there was no change. She looked at the rose stem every day but there was no change. “Oh, I (4) give up. Mum must have been joking,” she said and did not look at the rose stem anymore.

Three years later, Suzzanna became 11 years old in May. She loved May because there were always many flowers in the large garden of her house. As there were also some trees and *bushes, many birds came to the garden every morning. She enjoyed watching the garden full of flowers and birds. She did not remember the rose.

One day, when Suzzanna was watching birds, a *robin came flying toward her and landed on her shoulder. She was so excited. Then the robin flew away toward the *shaded spot. She followed the robin and came to the shaded part of the garden. She didn’t come to this part of the garden as it was quite large in size. She looked at it and said, “Wow! (5) ( I / grown / the rose / planted / that / has )” She planted only one stem but now there were some roses.

Two years later, Suzzanna was now 13 years old. The roses grew well and they were in full bloom. She was so glad to see it. Then she remembered (6) (see) the elderly woman. She said to herself, “I want her to see these roses! She may come to the park for a walk with her dog.”

Suzzanna went to the park the next morning because she thought that the woman might be there. She waited for fifteen minutes and she was lucky enough to see the woman and her dog. She walked to the woman and said, “Excuse me, but do you remember me?” The woman looked *confused because Suzzanna was grown up. “Some years ago, you gave me a rose,” said Suzzanna. “Oh, yes. I’m sorry I didn’t *recognise you because you are a tall girl now.” “I want to tell you the rose has grown and there are many roses. Can you come to my garden?”

Suzzanna and the elderly woman walked with the dog toward her house and she showed the rose to the woman. The woman was pleased to see the rose blossoms and said, “I didn’t expect the rose would grow. Thank you very much.” Her dog was excited to run in the large garden. Then the woman said, “By the way, do you like dogs?” Suzzanna said, “Yes, I (7) do. I love them!” “I’m going to France on holiday for two weeks. Would you and your parents be interested in looking after my dog, Mary, when I’m away?” said the woman. Suzzanna was excited and said, “Of course! I would love to look after Mary!” Suzzanna was old enough to look after a dog and she was sure that her mother would say yes.
